Keep your distance. Hold the beam on the Walker for 4-7 uninterrupted seconds. It continues approaching until the light drives it away. Losing the beam resets the exposure. Inside 1.5 metres, run: the beam cannot repel it.

If it stays closer than 1.5 metres for 3 continuous seconds, you die, even while walking. It moves faster than a walk but slower than a sprint.

Dry clicks are its footsteps. The surveyor left an axe beside the first body; two strikes kill a diseased wolf.

Marked amber shelters are safe. The research station’s bulbs and blue containment light are not.

The pale trail runs east to the storehouse. The fuse lies on its desk.

The longer return passes the old amber lantern. The abandoned research station has three rooms off a corridor, but its weak bulb is not shelter.

The surveyor took a map of every landmark. Last seen by the first bend north of this cabin.

Paths remain stable even when the trees seem to move.

It waited at the edge for an hour. The pale torso rose above eight jointed legs. No eyes. No nose. A mouth where a face should be.

The clicking stopped when I aimed the beam. When I looked down to replace the cell, it started on my left.

Keep a fresh battery for the way home. Recover only in a marked shelter.

The map is beside my coat. It marks the cabin, fuse storehouse, research station, old lantern, northern gate and the bodies we found. Distances are estimates.

Take my axe. The wolves no longer behave like animals. The blade will stop them; the Walker is something else.

Do not trust the research station’s dim lamp. It is too weak.

Three clicks, then silence. It was farther away than I thought. The sound returned faster, lower, beside the path.

Its jaw unhinged as it came closer. Rows of teeth kept unfolding beneath the blank crown.

The howls beyond the fence belong to wolves. The dry knocking between the trees does not.

STATION 03 / R-09

The archive holds eyes, embryos and animal heads in preservative. R-09 remains in the blue tank. The gate key hangs from the chain around its neck. Do not reach for it while the specimen is alive.

The red release control starts a five-second siren and drain. The doors then open. It does not fear the hand light. Four firearm hits or axe strikes stop it. Two strikes from it within five seconds are fatal. After death, recover the flashing key from the neck chain.

Restore the fuse circuit, then turn the recovered key in the separate lock beside the starting cabin panel. The weak station bulbs offer no shelter.

I can see the gate. Without the service circuit its switch is dead. Take the fuse back to the cabin first.

I counted the steps behind me. Eight feet, one rhythm. When it was near, even the forest wind disappeared beneath the pounding.

If the lamps come back on, follow them north. Do not stop for me.
Field axe acquired. Left mouse: swing. Two hits kill an undead wolf. Keep the Walker at a distance.

Mr. Norton,

They have crossed onto my land. Last night the lamps went out, but the things beneath them kept moving. Dead men's heads, crawling on six legs. One of them spoke in my brother's voice. He has been buried for nine years.

You are the finest hunter I know. I have left my shotgun beside the car. Light will not turn these creatures back. Use steel and shot. When their mouths begin to glow, get out of the way.

Please deal with them before they reach the houses. There is scratching under my door now.

E. Mercer
Blackpine ranger

Am I the only one who still can't believe what they're paying us?
If you feel guilty, I'll happily take your cut.
Not a chance. One night's work, a month's pay. What could go wrong?
Doesn't it bother you they never said what we're hunting?
Wildlife. That's what the contract said.
It also said no phones. You're all fine with that?
They paid half up front. For that money, I'd leave my pants at home.
Look at that gate... Since when do you need a fence like that for boars?
Maybe the boars around here hate visitors.
